chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Muhrim (person in Ihram) does not eat locusts."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram eat locusts?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that locusts are exempt from the general prohibition on hunting and eating game while in the state of Ihram, a ruling supported by the consensus of Shia jurists. It highlights the distinction between wild game (which is prohibited) and specific permitted animals like locusts, emphasizing the precision of fiqh in ritual purity and dietary laws during pilgrimage.
